summary: Iteration 10 — Export polish (PDF/Excel/CSV). Backend only. All 8 new export tests in /app/backend/tests/test_exports_v2.py PASS + full regression /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py 25/25 PASS (serial, ~50s). Verified: (1) Party PDF — content-type application/pdf, %PDF magic, FreeSans font embedded (byte-level 'FreeSans' present in the PDF stream — proves the bundled TTF replaced Helvetica), extracted text contains ₹ (U+20B9) in 'Closing balance: ₹…', headers 'Debit (₹)', 'Credit (₹)', 'Balance (₹)', plus 'Ledger Statement', 'Opening Balance', 'Total', the ledger name, and Dr/Cr suffixes; NO black-box (■) or replacement (\ufffd) chars. (2) Cash PDF — headers 'In (₹)' / 'Out (₹)' / 'Balance (₹)', closing text contains 'cash in hand'; multi-page: first-page and last-page footers both contain 'Generated by Munsiji' and 'Page N'; Indian-grouped numbers present in the extracted text; still uses FreeSans; no black-box. (3) Long-note wrapping — created EXPTEST_<r> party ledger via /api/groups[0].id, posted a ~180-char note ('lambi note wali entry ' repeated), exported PDF returned 200 and the beginning of the long note appears in extracted text (wrap not clip); cleanup DELETE succeeded — 0 EXPTEST_* leftovers. (4) Party Excel — A1 == '<ledger> — Ledger Statement', header row exactly ['Date','Particulars','Debit (₹)','Credit (₹)','Balance (₹)'], freeze_panes set below header row, column B width == 46 (≥40), Total row has numeric int/float cells with number_format '#,##0.00;[Red]-#,##0.00', Total.debit == /statement.total_debit, Total.credit == /statement.total_credit, Total.balance == /statement.closing_balance, last row 'Closing: ₹…' with the rupee sign. Cash Excel — header uses 'In (₹)' / 'Out (₹)'. (5) CSV — content-type text/csv, UTF-8 BOM present (0xEF 0xBB 0xBF), party header 'Date,Particulars,Debit,Credit,Balance', cash header 'Date,Particulars,In,Out,Balance', Total row has raw 2-decimal numbers. (6) WhatsApp bot — POST /api/whatsapp/simulate {'text':'Biki mill ka ledger pdf bhejo'} returned a files[] with a URL; downloading yields a valid PDF containing 'FreeSans' + ₹, no black box. Provider is MOCKED (wa_outbox), which is expected per test_credentials.md. Ran with pypdf 6.18 (installed) + openpyxl 3.1.5. No source changes required.
critical_code_review_comments: exports.py:32-41 (_register_fonts): correctly falls back to Helvetica if TTFs missing but the fonts are present (/app/backend/fonts/FreeSans*.ttf) and the guarded registerFont() call prevents duplicate registration across requests — verified 'FreeSans' shows up in the raw PDF bytes.

exports.py:44-59 (inr): Indian grouping is correct — matches the 2-2-3 tail pattern (28,07,120.00). Handles negatives via abs() so the sign must come from _bal_label or a separate marker; that is fine because Dr/Cr / (minus) are the display convention here.
exports.py:69-72 (_safe_text): neutralises spreadsheet formula injection by prefixing with a single quote for values starting with = + - @ \t \r — good defensive practice for user-supplied notes.

exports.py:267 (Table colWidths): 22+74+27+27+32 mm = 182 mm = A4 usable width, so no overflow. repeatRows=1 keeps header on every page. Wrapping Paragraph cells with fixed column widths fully solves 'lines aage peeche' issue.
exports.py:210 (freeze_panes below header row) and:208 (widths [13,46,16,16,18]) meet the spec (col B ≥ 40) — verified.
exports.py:135 (num_fmt '#,##0.00;[Red]-#,##0.00') matches the requested Excel number_format contract exactly.
exports.py:291-297 (footer): uses the same registered TTF (FreeSans) at 8pt for 'Generated by Munsiji · <ts>' and 'Page N' — both appear on page 1 and last page of the multi-page cash PDF.

rca_of_issue: Original bug — black-box for ₹ + misaligned lines — root cause was ReportLab's default Helvetica lacking the U+20B9 glyph plus lack of cell wrapping in fixed-width columns. Fix (verified): register bundled GNU FreeSans TTFs (fonts/FreeSans.ttf, FreeSansBold.ttf) which have the glyph, and use ReportLab Paragraph inside Table cells with explicit A4-safe column widths (22/74/27/27/32 mm). Byte-level check 'FreeSans' in the PDF stream + extracted-text checks for ₹ and absence of ■/\ufffd conclusively confirm the fix.
